paper.title_en: Fisher information in the flux landscape
paper.abstract_en: We quantify the fine-tuning of the flux superpotential in Type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifold compactifications using the Fisher Information Metric. Treating the background fluxes as model parameters and the magnitude of the superpotential as the physical observable, we show that the Fisher matrix admits a unique non-zero eigenvalue that bounds the superpotential from above and factorises into axio-dilaton, complex structure components and a bounded factor depending on both moduli and the phase of the superpotential. In the canonical duality frame and over the full flux lattice, this eigenvalue grows linearly with the inverse string coupling and cubically with the complex structure saxions. Specialising to a two modulus orientifold of the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^4(1,1,1,6,9)$ at large complex structure, we combine the flux integrality with the D3-brane tadpole condition to show that several flux components, including the one driving this growth, are forced to vanish across deep moduli space patches, truncating the twelve-dimensional flux lattice to an eight-dimensional sublattice. The Fisher eigenvalue restricted to these admissible flux directions either approaches a constant or grows at most linearly, much more slowly than over the full lattice.
